Yes. If by “experimental” you mean less polished ad creative, more culturally native, weird, participatory, creator-led, or street-level content, there are several Toronto shops I’d put ahead of conventional social agencies.

My shortlist

FUSE Create — probably the strongest fit if you want actual creative experimentation, not just TikTok-style edits. They explicitly do social stunts, UGC/influencer work, online video and “stuntvertising”; their Ricola work, for example, played with the conventions of social ad units. 
CRUEL

We Are Social Toronto — strongest if you want internet culture rather than traditional advertising. They're a social-first creative agency, and their Canadian work includes campaigns built around viral TikTok moments. 
Good Kids

Super Duper Studios — interesting if your shop wants creator-led, culturally specific campaigns. Their Ruffles work deliberately used debate/comment-section engagement, while their PepsiCo TikTok launch combined creators with physical activations.

StreetTalk — a particularly good option if you want to make your shop feel native to Toronto rather than like a brand broadcasting at Toronto. They specialize in street interviews, genuine reactions and social-first edits for TikTok/Reels/Shorts. 
StreetTalk

Taste - A Brand Experience Agency — worth looking at if you're a food, beverage, hospitality or lifestyle shop. They combine social content with real-world experiences, pop-ups, creators and local media.

Viterno Group — the most performance/volume-oriented experimental option I found. They're unusually focused on short-form, claiming 300M+ organic views and showing substantial client Reel/TikTok results. 
Viterno Group

If I were your shop…

I'd not brief an agency with “make our Instagram more creative.” That's how you get another beautiful carousel and a Reel with trending audio.

I'd tell them:

“Our ads currently look like ads. We want ideas that people would watch even if they didn't know who paid for them.”

Then ask each agency for 3 genuinely weird concepts for your shop, with no requirement that the concepts be polished or traditionally brand-safe. You'll learn much more from those pitches than from their agency reels.

My first three calls would be FUSE Create, We Are Social, and StreetTalk—but for a small local retailer, StreetTalk may actually be the most immediately actionable.

If you tell me what kind of Toronto shop you run (fashion, food, beauty, furniture, specialty retail, etc.) and roughly your monthly content/ads budget, I can narrow this to 3 agencies and show you the kind of experimental concepts each could make for you.
